open.heading:
A pattern,
{{not a policy.}}
body: The school states one thing about homework: that it is **set to a published pattern** rather than assigned subject by subject on the day. That is the whole of it, and the whole of it is what appears here.

No minutes per night, no days per subject, no weekend rule, no holiday rule — because none of those is published, and a family that plans its evenings around an invented figure would be planning around us rather than around the school.

item.kicker: Where the question is actually answered
item.heading:
Item five,
{{and item eleven.}}
body: The more useful fact is not on the school’s homework page at all — it is projected on a screen in its Parents’ Forum. The agenda runs to **twelve items**, and two of them are this subject.

A parent who wants to know how much homework is set, and whether it comes back marked, has a standing item on a published agenda to raise it under. That is a better answer than a paragraph describing a policy this site cannot verify.

body: Steps three and four describe a published *channel* — the forum agenda — rather than a rule about marking turnaround, because the school publishes the channel and not the rule.

clear.heading:
Less guessing.
{{More clarity.}}
body: Homework at Sunbeam follows the school’s published approach. Where there is a question about it, the three places on the right are where it can be put — and each of them is a channel the school names itself.

gap.heading:
What the page
{{doesn’t pretend to know.}}
body: Each of the four was checked for on the school’s site and is genuinely absent. We do not assume, estimate or invent any of them.

ask.kicker: When a question needs an answer
ask.heading:
Ask the school,
{{not the assumption.}}
body: The Parents’ Forum, parent–teacher interaction and the school office are the three channels the school names. Between them they cover homework practice, feedback, correction and the support that follows.
Meeting dates are on the [parent–teacher meetings](/academics/assessment/parent-teacher-meetings/) page; the office line is on [Contact](/contact-us/).

close.heading:
Published clearly.
{{Discussed openly.}}
body: The school publishes that homework follows a pattern, and gives parents two standing agenda items to raise it under. The pattern itself — the load, the days, the weekend and holiday rules — is not published anywhere on its site, and nothing has been invented to fill the gap.
